claim: The new wrapper now drops every diagnostic whose location is not in source in this compilation. That includes `Location.None`, which results whenever helpers such as `GetIdentifierLocation`, `GetLocation(IParameterSymbol)` or `GetParameterListLocation` return null for types declared in the compiling assembly. Before the change those diagnostics were still reported (without location); now real errors on in-assembly types can silently disappear. This contradicts 'types declared in the same assembly keep working as before'.

claim:
The new helper `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` still indexes `property.DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` without a guard. Its XML doc says it returns null for metadata properties, but it throws `IndexOutOfRangeException` instead. It also hard-casts to `PropertyDeclarationSyntax`, which fails for positional record properties.

Concrete input: a `[MessagePackObject] public struct Item<T>` in a referenced assembly with `[Key((string)null)] public string Key { get; set; }`, used as `Item<int>` from a `[MessagePackObject]` type in the app. `CollectGeneric` runs `GetObjectInfo` on the metadata type and reaches the `intKey == null && stringKey == null` branch. In analyzer mode `reportDiagnostic` is non-null, so the `Invoke` argument is evaluated and the helper throws before `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` can drop the diagnostic. The result is AD0001, the same crash this requirement is meant to remove.
